answer: Distributed verifiers resist Sybils by sending unpredictable nonces and measuring round-trip echo latencies to triangulate each agent's region and throttle colocated keys. Because virtual clones on one server share matching delay cones, an attacker must rent physically dispersed hosts or residential uplinks per identity. Asymmetric routing and packet jitter still corrupt these bounds, risking false rejections for remote nodes such as a wildlife sensor logging a whisper from a sable.
